content:
anya: quick heads-up — a customer hit us with PII leakage in debug payloads (emails) after requests routed through legacy proxy. seems like ordering of scrub vs routing-affinity is wrong. anyone seen this pattern before?

samir: ugh. which pipeline? request-logger or ingress-router?

anya: request-logger -> legacy-proxy -> route-assignment. logger is supposed to redact, but the proxy attaches `X-Route` before we scrub, and our scrub is route-aware.

lina: ah so redact depends on route rules and the proxy is adding the route afterwards. if we rely on route for redaction level, we might leak.

marta: can we flip to always redact before any header-based routing? that feels safest but may increase false-positive redaction and hurt debuggability.

samir: agreed safest. trade-off: harder to correlate logs with routes for debugging. we already have per-tenant redaction profiles.

anya: proposal: make two passes — prefix-scrub (aggressive) before routing, then enriched-scrub (route-specific) after routing. prefix-scrub uses smaller ruleset (emails, ssn, keys).

devex: UX concern: prefix-scrub will make Console’s request inspector show redacted request body for most quicklook cases. folks will complain they can’t see minimal fields when debugging.

ops-bot: reminder: quota events spike when double-scrub runs on high-throughput tenants.

samir: good point. performance impact matters. we also have autoscaling thresholds that trigger when per-token CPU hits X. double-scrub could push some queues.

taylor: what about a hybrid: prefix-scrub enabled for tenants with `consent_propagation=false` or for routes marked `ingress_untrusted=true`. for others, single pass with route-aware rules.

marta: tenants rarely set `consent_propagation`. ops teams can add a tenant tag though. but some customers rely on our default.

anya: another option: move route assignment earlier in the pipeline (as early as possible) so routing header exists before scrub, but only if header is trustworthy. we can have the legacy proxy attest the route with an HMAC header `X-Route-Signature` and we validate it.

lina: signature validation increases complexity but might be best — keeps single scrub pass and preserves debug visibility. legacy proxy changes required.

samir: timeline: proxy changes = weeks. HMAC rollout = risky. hybrid approach seems pragmatic: prefix-scrub for chatty public routes + HMAC plan as medium-term.

devex: also add a Console flag to show "raw (redacted-first)" vs "routed view" — make it clear why fields differ. reduces help-desk volume.

anya: agree. also need telemetry: count how many requests had prefix-scrub applied and any leakage incidents. create a dashboard tile: `prefix_scrub_rate` and `post_scrub_leak_detected`.

ops-bot: quota note: if prefix-scrub increases CPU by ~15% per-token, tagging tenants will help route them into Dedicated pools automatically. we can tie to routing policies.

marta: can we sketch a minimal config change? something like:
```yaml
scrub_pipeline:
  - name: prefix_scrub
    ruleset: core_safe
    enabled: true
  - name: route_scrub
    ruleset: tenant_route_profiles
    enabled: true
routing:
  accept_signed_route: true
  signature_header: X-Route-Signature
```

samir: looks good. need to ensure `core_safe` includes emails, credit-card numbers, api-keys, basic PII. not NLP-level redaction.

lina: will open a tiny RFC for ruleset `core_safe` contents. low false positives, high recall for big PII classes.

devex: for Console, we should show an inline tooltip: "Redaction applied before routing to prevent accidental leaks. Click to view redaction evidence." and an action to request temporary inspector-unmask with audit logging.

anya: policy Qs: do we allow on-call to temporarily disable prefix-scrub for a tenant? that sounds risky. previous incidents show misuse.

marta: I'd prefer a breakglass flow but only for SRE+Legal approval and must record a per-request audit. UI should require a justification string.

samir: breakglass ok but implement TTL short (5m) and tenant-level audit record. ops must notify the customer.

lina: agreed. add a telemetry counter `breakglass_usage` and alert if >3 in 24h for a tenant.

devex: final point — update SDK docs: explain `ingress_untrusted` and `accept_signed_route`. also mention potential Console view diffs.

anya: action items:
- lina: RFC for `core_safe` ruleset (due EOD Wed)
- samir: perf estimate for double-scrub vs signature flow (due Mon)
- marta: prototype Console flag + breakglass UI copy (due Fri)
- devex: docs snippet and tooltip text (due Thu)
- ops: add dashboard tiles: `prefix_scrub_rate`, `post_scrub_leak_detected`, `breakglass_usage` (due Mon)

marta: acked, I'll start a runbook stub for breakglass.

samir: I'll look at whether we can offload prefix-scrub to the edge function (cheaper) for high-volume tenants.

anya: thanks all. if anyone sees a customer incident that looks like this please ping with example request id. I'll reroute to this thread. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: noted. Created incident tag `P-PRIVACY-ROUTE-01` for tracking.
